x-m-el-econ-04.title: If Price Go Up, Profit Really Grow?

x-m-el-econ-04.s.s1.prompt: Owner talk, 'The higher the price, the more money remain for each cup, so profit go keep growing too.' What be the strongest evidence to prove this claim wrong?

x-m-el-econ-04.s.s1.r.a: This value only show the limit where profit start to be 0 or more; e no tell wetin happen if price keep going up.

x-m-el-econ-04.s.s1.r.b: You use clear numbers show say even if profit for each cup increase, amount wey fit sell decrease.
x-m-el-econ-04.s.s1.o.c: If price na 1,500 won, profit for each cup na 0 won, so selling no increase profit.
x-m-el-econ-04.s.s1.r.c: This one na about low price. E go against the claim 'the higher e go.'
x-m-el-econ-04.s.s1.o.d: If ingredient cost rise, money wey remain from each cup go reduce.
x-m-el-econ-04.s.s1.r.d: That true, but e no concern claim about raising price.
x-m-el-econ-04.s.s1.explain: At price 7,000원, maximum sales na 1,400 − 1,400 = 0 cups. Even if profit per cup na 5,500원, if nothing sell, profit na −1,200,000원. Claim look only at one thing (profit per cup) and forget sales.
x-m-el-econ-04.s.s2.prompt: Make 2 (price, sales) pairs with different prices where monthly profit na 0원 or more. Price dey in units of 100원, sales na integer and must no pass maximum sales.

x-m-el-econ-04.s.s2.fail.c3: E pass maximum number of cups wey fit sell at that price.

x-m-el-econ-04.s.s2.explain: For p=3500, maximum na 700 cups, and 650 cups × 2,000 = 1,300,000 ≥ 1,200,000. For p=4000, maximum na 600 cups, and 500 × 2,500 = 1,250,000. Prices wey fit work, in units of 100원, dey from 3,000원 to 5,500원.
x-m-el-econ-04.s.s2.because.prompt: Write one sentence each to explain why no combination with profit 0 or more dey when price too low or too high.
x-m-el-econ-04.s.s2.because.hint.0: Write how profit per cup and amount sold each change as price rise.
x-m-el-econ-04.s.s2.because.hint.1: The product of the two factors must pass fixed cost.

x-m-el-econ-04.s.s2.because.model.0: If price too low, money left per cup small, so even if you sell all you fit sell, e no cover fixed cost 1,200,000원. If price too high, cup sales go down, so even if profit per cup big, total profit no reach.

x-m-el-econ-06.s.s2.model.0: Since 3,000원 remain per bar, break-even point na 600,000 ÷ 3,000 = 200 bars. If 120 sell, you earn 3,000 × 120 = 360,000원, wey fall short of fixed cost 600,000원 by 240,000원, so loss na 240,000원. Dividing by 5,000원 ignore say 2,000원 ingredient cost don go out.

x-m-el-econ-01.title: Simple and Compound Interest: Which One Better, and When?
x-m-el-econ-01.goal: Compare two deposits with different rates and interest methods in a table; explain with evidence the conditions where "compound interest always better" hold.
x-m-el-econ-01.material:

Product B: compound interest, 3.5% per year; each year interest adds to principal and next year's interest is based on it.

2 years | 1,080,000 | 1,071,225
4 years | 1,160,000 | 1,147,523
6 years | 1,240,000 | 1,229,255
8 years | 1,320,000 | 1,316,809
10 years | 1,400,000 | 1,410,599
12 years | 1,480,000 | 1,511,069
